summary.title: Predictable Delivery
summary.one_liner: A slide deck by Matthew Story on why product and engineering teams struggle to deliver predictably, and how measuring delivery (rather than effort alone) and using data can help, with caveats about data.
takeaways: Product and engineering teams often measure different things: engineering tends to track effort (estimate-based velocity), while product tracks delivery (roadmaps, deadlines, sprint attainment).
Consistently missing goals is demotivating, and predictability is a core concern for managers.
The deck outlines a simple 'poor man's predictability' approach before moving to using data.
Data-driven predictability has its own problems, which the author explicitly discusses.
summary.summary: This is a slide deck (Google Slides, view-only) by Matthew Story, founder of DirectorOf.Me, presented as a talk on predictable delivery for product and engineering (P&E) teams. The agenda covers what P&E teams do, how to measure it, the problem with predictability, a low-effort approach called "poor man's predictability," using data, and the problems with data. The slides are mostly short text bullets with a few quotes and the author's background, so the detailed content of each agenda section is not present in the extracted text.
